resources.string: Set up and launch Linux, EmulationStation and PortMaster
Run a Linux system on your console alongside andr36oid. dArkOSen is the recommended starting point: use EmulationStation and PortMaster to play ports, then exit the subsystem to return to Android.

This runs a Linux rootfs, such as dArkOSen, in a separate contained environment, a bit like Docker. With full handoff, Android\'s heavy background services are stopped first, so all of your open Android apps are closed while it runs. Speed should be close to running the custom firmware on its own, but it uses the andr36oid kernel, so a few things may not behave exactly as expected. Your EASYROMS partition, or the data partition if you chose not to create EASYROMS, is mounted inside the custom firmware as /roms.
Linux rootfs image found. Ready to launch.
No Linux image found. Copy the dArkOSen image to your games card, or choose an image in Advanced mode.
Open the EASYROMS (games) drive on your games card. Create a folder named subsystem/darkosen/ and put the dArkOSen .img file inside it. If the image is compressed, extract it first.
Use the official Install.Full.PortMaster.sh to install PortMaster into tools/PortMaster/ on the same card. The full installer is recommended because it works offline.
Put ports in the ports/ folder on the same card. Open EmulationStation or PortMaster below. Exit the subsystem to return to Android.

Launch EmulationStation to play, or PortMaster to manage your ports. These launches use the automatically detected image. A full handoff gives Linux the screen and closes your Android apps. Save your work before launching.\n\nUse Setup steps to prepare your games card, Settings to choose what starts at boot, or Advanced mode for other Linux images and a live boot console.

You can complete setup entirely offline. Copy an extracted .img file using a computer, insert the card, then choose Check again. A download is offered only when this device has an Internet connection.
These are steps you carry out on the games card. This wizard checks for a rootfs image; it does not install PortMaster or verify your ports.

Your Linux image has been found. Finish setup to choose EmulationStation or PortMaster.\n\nWith full handoff, launching closes Android apps and hands the display to Linux. Save your Android work first. Exit Linux to return to Android.
Boot into the subsystem by default
Choose whether your console starts in Android or the Linux subsystem. When the switch is off, it starts in Android. Choose the Linux app to open when the subsystem starts automatically.
Hold START at boot to start the other OS, regardless of your default.
Could not save the setting. Try again.

Choose a compatible Linux rootfs image and how it shares the console with Android. Other images must support the andr36oid kernel and this subsystem.\n\nKeep Android running to inspect the boot log without giving Linux the screen. This is useful for troubleshooting; graphical Linux apps may require full handoff.
Linux will take over the display. Android background services will stop and your open Android apps will close. Save your work before continuing. Exit Linux to return to Android.
Android stays on screen. Launch to watch the live Linux boot console. This mode does not hand the display to graphical Linux apps.
Hold A, Enter, or the ring for 3 seconds to confirm. Release early to cancel.

Browse your EASYROMS games card, SD2, USB, or a subsystem folder on mounted storage. Choose an extracted, non-empty .img file. Compressed images and unfinished downloads are hidden.\n\nThe full path must fit the system property limit of 91 UTF-8 bytes. Back goes up a folder; at the storage list it returns to Advanced mode.
